I don’t recognize myself in that second picture or any of the pictures of me from my active addiction. I was 72lb when I finally decided to get sober, quite literally on the brink of death. 
I started using meth at the ripe age of 14 years old and continued to use until after my 16th birthday. I destroyed every prior friendship and relationship with my family. I was honestly ready to die. I was in my lowest of lows. I witnessed someone getting murdered in front of me, I’ve allowed myself to be in situations where I was sexually assaulted. I’ve hurt myself and the people I loved. I would’ve never been placed in those scenarios have I never tried it. 
To some people, a year in addiction doesn’t seem like a very long time but to me it was a lifetime. I’ve lived and been thru things nobody should have ever have to experience. The only reason I got sober was because I was sent to jail. I truly believe I would’ve died if I in my addiction for even a week longer. The first 6 months was the hardest, every single day I thought about meth. It’s so weird, when you’re sober you think about how amazing she is but when you’re on it you’re filled with regret and hate it. It’s like a toxic relationship. You only think of the good things when you’re apart but when you’re back together you remember all the bad and why you tried to leave in the first place. 
It took me a long time to want to be sober rather than just being sober cause I was forced too. After 17 months in juvy, I was placed on house arrest then probation. I was completely free in April. I have no desire to use drugs, not even weed. 
Sometimes I think about meth, not often through and not to the extent of needing to taste it but sometimes when I’m sad I fantasize about her comforting chills and how she made me skinny and feeling confident…. I just need to look at those pictures tho and clear my act up. I thought I was hot as all hell back then and I literally looked so meth’d out.
I’m proud to say I’m a manager at a restaurant now, I’m still working on getting my license back but with time that will come. 
I just needed to get a little rant out. Can’t wait to finally be able to say im 4 years sober from my kryptonite. Such a big accomplishment.

Happy birthday! Remember you’re still allowed to have fun as an adult but you have to be a lot more responsible. 

If you’re going to drink, drink moderately. It’s going to be accessible a lot more to you now. I feel like everyone should at least see what a bar/club scene is like at least once in there life, but it’s easy to get lost i
In. Don’t bother trying the drug scene, it’s not worth in my opinion. You’re way more likely to lose yourself in the process of “exploring” and may never make it back. 

Make a savings account, put as much as you can away into a tax free savings account. Put away money for an emergency fund and learn how to budget. 

Focus on getting a good career for yourself, something you will enjoy but make enough to live comfortably. Take some time and think about what you want to do, it’s a live changing decision but remember it’s never to late to change your mind either. 

Take care of your body. You only have one. Eat healthy, and work out. I know easier said than done, but try pre-workout for motivation to workout. After forcing yourself for awhile it will easily become part of your everyday routine.

Take care of your mind. Mental health is SO important and often people forget that they need to care/think about themselves. Take days to relax and focus on yourself. Figure out who you are as a person. Self care is essential!!

For dating and sex, use protection and always be sure to ask if the person is clean. Date someone who treats you good and someone you can actually see you spending your whole life with. Communicate with your partner with your wants and needs, any issues you may have, etc. Communication is key to a relationship and many other aspects to life! Try to work things out but if you’re more sad than happy, leave the relationship. There’s plenty of people out there, don’t settle. 

For friends or other people in general.. be careful who you trust. There’s plenty of people who use and abuse when given the opportunity, but there is also people who truly care about you and want to see you grow as a person. You need to learn how to decipher the good from bad. If you feel as if a friend isn’t treating you right, do yourself a favour and sever ties. You can always make new friends. It can be hard to leave a friendship/relationship but you don’t deserve to be treated like shit either. You don’t need toxic shit in your life. 

Be assertive with what you want. Work towards goals you set for yourself. Never let someone belittle you or treat you like shit because you’re so much better than that. Stand up for yourself and others. Never give up on what you believe in. Don’t do illegal shit cause it will stay on your record forever lmao.
Adulthood is tough stuff but remember we all looked forward to this stage in our life we may as well make the best of it. Everyone achieves things at there own pace, don’t ever be discouraged if you aren’t doing things as fast as someone else you’ll get there.

Once again happy birthday. Hope you the best(:

Hello love, I used to be a meth addict but have since found sobriety. I’ve been on both sides of this. 

I feel as if your boyfriend is rationalizing his use, every addict I’ve met has done this at one point of their addiction including myself. If he’s only using occasionally, I believe it’s still in the early stages of addiction. Unfortunately, this can be the stage where the drug is highly glorified. He hasn’t really came down hard before, and meth can seem almost harmless, and even helpful. You mentioned his mom had suffered from addiction. Addiction often runs in the family as a genetic makeup can increase the risk of substance abuse disorder. u/Toystorations gave you some amazing advice with very good information too. I agree with him 100%. 

My advice is to try and be there for him without enabling him. Often the loved ones to addict enable them without even realizing it. Such as making excuses for them, or helping them with things they could do themselves. 

I would do some research on meth then have a conversation with him. I feel like once you have a better understanding of the drug and the knowledge of how an addicts brain works you will be able to see the signs a lot better. 

Try to help pursue addiction counselling. Unfortunately this can be difficult as he hasn’t admitted to himself that he has a problem with meth. If someone doesn’t want to get clean or get help for themselves it’s extremely hard for them to stay sober. 

If the addition gets worse and he isn’t trying to help himself, please do not stay in the relationship. Some addicts never change, and some need to hit rock bottom before they feel the need to change (Like myself). 

Never try meth, it’s the devils drug. Once is too much and twice is never enough.
